questions.question: When getting ready to change lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your side mirror.
Check your rearview mirror.
Turn your head quickly to check for other vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors for vehicles behind you. Just before you move, turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. This warns other drivers and helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: Nighttime is the safest time for cyclists to ride their bikes.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Bicycles are hard to see in the dark, even with lights and reflectors. Both drivers and cyclists should be extra careful at night to prevent crashes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
No trucks are allowed on the upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you about a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.
Speed up to cross the tracks before the gate is lowered.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Not pay attention to how many tracks there are to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop for any trains or vehicles on the tracks.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal before you change lanes or move your vehicle right or left. Check your mirrors and turn your head to see your blind spot before making any side-to-side move.

questions.question: If a road is slippery, maintain a following distance that is:

options.text: No different than normal.
Farther from the car ahead than normal.
Closer to the car ahead than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther from the car ahead than normal.
questions.explanation: On a slippery road, it takes longer to stop. Keep a longer distance between your car and the car ahead.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Is loose.
Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Is hidden beneath the seat.
Keeps the seat belt buzzer or light from operating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable and allow your fist to fit between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: If you are driving and you see animals standing near the roadway:

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down and proceed with caution if you see animals near the road. They may suddenly move into your path. There may be more animals hidden from view.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Merge.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: What is the safe way to cross railroad tracks?

options.text: Look both ways, but only when the red light is flashing.
Listen and look both ways. Only cross if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen and look both ways. Only cross if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Before crossing, listen and look both ways for trains. Watch for warning signals. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: By looking in your side mirrors.
By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
By looking in your rearview mirror.
By staring straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulders to check them.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you drive. Also adjust your seat, fasten your belt, and secure items before moving your vehicle. Do not adjust mirrors while driving.

questions.question: Must drivers give the right-of-way to pedestrians with disabilities using guide dogs, white canes, or other devices?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Pedestrians with disabilities using guide dogs, white canes, wheelchairs, or other devices have the right-of-way. They have the same rights as any other pedestrian.

questions.question: Which statement is true about railroad crossings?

options.text: You should use cruise control near a railroad crossing to keep a steady speed.
You must stop when a flagger or stop sign tells you to at a railroad crossing.
You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop when a flagger or stop sign tells you to at a railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Always be careful near railroad tracks.

questions.question: What is the best way to change lanes?

options.text: Quickly and often.
When a car is in your blind spot.
Gradually and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually and carefully.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes gradually and carefully. Only change lanes when necessary. Every lane change increases the risk of an accident.

questions.question: What should you do when driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.
Take the right-of-way.
Drive normally.
Speed up and drive away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: What must you do when a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone?

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow normal traffic laws instead of the flagger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the flagger's directions.
questions.explanation: Follow the flagger's directions. Slow down when told. Not obeying is illegal and dangerous to workers in construction zones.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
Slippery when wet.
Road curves ahead.
You are approaching a hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does excessive speed do?

options.text: Saves time and gets you there faster.
Helps you get around obstacles.
Increases the risk of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a common cause of crashes. It does not save time and leads to dangerous decisions.

questions.question: When taking any medicine, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor about how it affects your driving.
Have someone follow you home.
Keep your window open and drive more slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor about how it affects your driving.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Always ask your doctor or pharmacist how a medicine will affect you before driving. This is especially important for tranquilizers and sedatives.

questions.question: If you are getting tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
Drink something with caffeine.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: To stay safe, take a break every hour on long trips. If possible, share driving with another person so you can rest while they drive.

questions.question: Night driving is difficult because:

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you can only see as far as your headlights shine. This makes it hard to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are going.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must stop completely and give the right-of-way to others.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and give the right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and give the right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means yield. Slow down when you see it and be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians go first if they are in your way.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help anyone who is hurt.
Call the police.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop right away. Move your car out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Help stop any serious bleeding. Wait for emergency workers to arrive.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only children have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.
questions.explanation: Develop a habit of buckling your seat belt before you start the car. Make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.
Always.
Only if a crossing guard is there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes (with or without a red tip).

questions.question: What happens when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: Both effects can get stronger.
Nothing happens.
Both effects can get weaker.
Only the alcohol effect gets weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both effects can get stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, one drink while taking a cold medicine can feel like you have had several drinks.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger tells you to stop.
There is a stop sign.
Red lights are flashing and gates are down.
Any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger signals you to stop, when there is a stop sign, or when red lights are flashing and gates are down.

questions.question: A driver taking an over-the-counter medicine should:

options.text: Read the label before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Keep driving no matter what the label says.
Drive only during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the label before driving.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter medicines like cold and allergy remedies can affect your driving. Always check the label for warnings. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if it is safe to drive.
